notes.title: BTEQ .RUN logon file
notes.text: Logon scripts are not carried over. The job runs as a Snowflake task under a service role, and credentials stay out of the code.

notes.title: MULTISET VOLATILE TABLE
notes.text: Rule-based rewrite to TEMPORARY TABLE. PRIMARY INDEX and ON COMMIT PRESERVE ROWS have no meaning in Snowflake and are dropped.

notes.title: SEL / DEL / INS abbreviations
notes.text: Expanded to SELECT / DELETE / INSERT.

notes.title: .IF ERRORCODE / .GOTO control flow
notes.text: BTEQ branches on the error code after each step. Devin wrapped the delete + insert in one transaction with an EXCEPTION handler, so a failed insert no longer leaves the table half-deleted. That was a latent bug in the legacy script.

notes.title: CAST ... AS DATE FORMAT
notes.text: The FORMAT clause only affects display in Teradata. event_ts arrives as TIMESTAMP_LTZ in Snowflake, so Devin converts to the business timezone first. A generated test covers the midnight boundary.

notes.title: COLLECT STATISTICS
notes.text: Removed. Snowflake does not need manual statistics. Left as a comment so reviewers can see it was dropped on purpose.

tests.name: Midnight timezone boundary maps to the right date

lines: SELECT s.return_id, s.reason_cd, ISNULL(s.refund_amount, 0) AS refund_amount,
SET t.reason_cd = s.reason_cd, t.refund_amount = s.refund_amount, t.updated_at = GETDATE()

notes.title: SELECT INTO #temp table
notes.text: The engine flagged SELECT ... INTO #temp as having no direct equivalent. Devin rewrote it as a session-scoped TEMPORARY TABLE built with CTAS, so it is dropped with the session the way #temp was.

notes.title: WITH (NOLOCK) hint
notes.text: Removed. Snowflake reads from a consistent snapshot, so the dirty-read hint is not needed. The PR description notes this as an intentional behavior change: no more uncommitted reads.

notes.title: TRY/CATCH block
notes.text: Mapped to a Snowflake Scripting EXCEPTION handler that wraps the whole body, so the temp-table build is covered too.

notes.title: @@ROWCOUNT after MERGE

lines: CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE SALES.load_order_daily IS
INSERT INTO SALES.fct_order (order_id, channel_cd, net_amount, bucket, load_dt)
LEFT JOIN SALES.fct_order t ON t.order_id = s.order_id
INSERT INTO SALES.fct_order (order_id, channel_cd, net_amount, bucket, load_dt)

notes.title: Row-by-row cursor loop
notes.text: Devin rewrote the FOR loop as one set-based INSERT ... SELECT. Same output, one statement instead of one round trip per row. A parity test compares it with the legacy output.

notes.title: SYSDATE / TRUNC(SYSDATE)
notes.text: Rule-based rewrite to CURRENT_TIMESTAMP() and CURRENT_DATE().

notes.title: DECODE
notes.text: Supported natively. Moved into the SELECT list as part of the set-based rewrite.

notes.title: NVL
notes.text: Supported natively. Kept as-is.

notes.title: Explicit COMMIT
notes.text: Dropped. The single INSERT ... SELECT is atomic, so a failure leaves no partial rows.

notes.title: DUP_VAL_ON_INDEX handler
notes.text: Snowflake does not enforce unique keys, so this exception would never fire and duplicates would slip through. Devin added an explicit check for duplicates in the batch and against keys already in the target. It raises the same error code (-20010) so downstream alerting still matches.

tests.name: Parity: set-based output equals cursor output

notes.title: CONNECT BY / SYS_CONNECT_BY_PATH
notes.text: Supported natively. Kept as-is.

notes.title: ROWNUM filter before hierarchy
notes.text: In Oracle, ROWNUM is applied before the tree is ordered, so which 5,000 rows came back was effectively random. Devin swapped it for a deterministic LIMIT after ordering and flagged the behavior change for the reviewer.

notes.title: CONNECT BY NOCYCLE
notes.text: NOCYCLE is not available. Devin added a data-quality test that fails if the seeded hierarchy contains a cycle, so a bad parent link is caught before the view runs.

notes.title: ORDER SIBLINGS BY
notes.text: Not supported. Ordering by the materialized path gives the same depth-first, alphabetical-within-parent order.

modules.name: rpt.vw_return_latest

lines: CASE WHEN l.last_refund_amount IS NULL THEN 'n/a'
ELSE CAST(l.last_refund_amount AS VARCHAR(20)) END AS display_value
SELECT TOP 1 e.refund_amount AS last_refund_amount, e.event_at AS last_event_at
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW rpt.vw_return_latest AS
CASE WHEN l.last_refund_amount IS NULL THEN 'n/a'
ELSE CAST(l.last_refund_amount AS VARCHAR(20)) END AS display_value
SELECT e.return_id, e.refund_amount AS last_refund_amount, e.event_at AS last_event_at
QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY e.return_id ORDER BY e.event_at DESC) = 1

notes.title: TOP 100 PERCENT in a view
notes.text: A SQL Server trick to allow ORDER BY in a view. It does not guarantee order and has no equivalent, so it is removed.

notes.title: CROSS APPLY (SELECT TOP 1 ...)
notes.text: Rewritten as an inner join to a QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() subquery. Like CROSS APPLY, it drops rows with no events. A test checks this.

notes.title: ORDER BY inside a view
notes.text: Dropped. Consumers sort explicitly. Devin checked the two seeded BI extracts that read this view, and both already have ORDER BY.
